title: Rational polynomial additive-bar contraction
statement:
For a commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra $B$ and an integer $r\geq0$, define the nonnegative cochain complex $P_{B,r}$ by
$$P_{B,r}^n=B[x_{a,i}:1\leq a\leq n,\ 1\leq i\leq r],\qquad n\geq0,$$
using polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Write $x_a=(x_{a,1},\ldots,x_{a,r})$. Its differential is
$$(df)(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})=f(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^{n}(-1)^a f(x_1,\ldots,x_a+x_{a+1},\ldots,x_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(x_1,\ldots,x_n).$$
In degree zero the first and last terms cancel. Put $P^n=0$ for $n<0$.

Let $K_{B,r}^q$ be the free $B$-module on $e_I$ for subsets $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ of cardinality $q$, with zero differential and zero terms for $q<0$ or $q>r$. Define $i:K_{B,r}\to P_{B,r}$ by $i(e_\varnothing)=1$ and
$$i(e_{\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}})=x_{1,i_1}\cdots x_{q,i_q}.$$
Define $p^0=1_B$. For $q>0$, define $p^q$ on a polynomial monomial to be zero unless every block $x_a$ has total degree one and these degree-one coordinates have pairwise distinct indices $j_1,\ldots,j_q$. In that remaining case set
$$p^q(x_{1,j_1}\cdots x_{q,j_q})=\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)e_{\{j_1,\ldots,j_q\}},$$
where $(j_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,j_{\sigma(q)})$ is increasingly ordered. Extend $B$-linearly. Then $d^2=0$, $di=0$, $pd=0$, $pi=1$, and there are $B$-linear maps $h^q:P_{B,r}^q\to P_{B,r}^{q-1}$ with
$$dh+hd=1-ip.$$
The maps $h$ can be chosen over $\mathbf Q$ and extended to every $B$: each rational monomial is sent to a finite rational linear combination of monomials, and all displayed identities hold after scalar extension. Thus this gives a chain homotopy equivalence, not only a list of cohomology groups. The zero algebra is allowed. For $r=0$, $i$ is the degree-zero inclusion of $B$ into the unnormalized constant cosimplicial complex.

proof.text: Work first over $\mathbf Q$. The coface substitutions are the ones from addition with unit $0$: omitting an outer variable and replacing adjacent variables by their sum. Applying two substitutions in either possible order agrees by associativity of addition and by its unit law; equivalently, for cofaces $\delta^a$, $\delta^b\delta^a=\delta^a\delta^{b-1}$ when $a<b$. In the expansion of $d^2$, each such composite occurs twice with opposite signs, so $d^2=0$. In degree zero $d=0$ as stipulated. Polynomial substitution and comparison on variables are legitimate by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of the rational polynomial-bar contraction; coface identities

proof.text: For $i(e_I)$, expand each substitution of $x_a+x_{a+1}$ by linearity of the single coordinate occurring in that block. The term choosing the right variable at position $a$ cancels the term choosing the left variable at position $a+1$; the two end terms cancel the first and last remaining terms. Hence $di=0$. To check $pd=0$, express $p^q(f)$ as the alternating wedge of the coefficient of degree one in each of the $q$ blocks, identifying the basis wedge with $e_I$. Outer cofaces omit a block and contribute zero. An inner coface can contribute only from degree two in its merged block and degree one in every other block. The two orders of two distinct coordinates have equal coefficients and opposite wedge signs; a repeated coordinate wedges to zero. Thus every contribution vanishes. Finally $pi(e_I)=e_I$, including the empty subset. These are coefficient calculations, so already hold over every $B$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of the rational polynomial-bar contraction; the prescribed i and p, with their signs

proof.text:
For a multi-index $m\in\mathbf N^r$, let $P_m^n$ be the span of monomials whose total exponent in coordinate $i$ across all blocks is $m_i$. All cofaces preserve $m$, and every polynomial is a finite sum of such homogeneous parts. In $P_m^n$ use the divided-monomial basis
$$b_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n}=\prod_{a,i}x_{a,i}^{\alpha_{a,i}}/\alpha_{a,i}!,\qquad \sum_a\alpha_a=m.$$
This is a finite basis in each degree. The binomial formula says that the middle coface replaces $\alpha_a$ by all pairs $\beta+\gamma=\alpha_a$, each with coefficient $1$ in this basis; the two outer cofaces insert a zero block. The codegeneracies set one block equal to zero, killing its positive-degree monomials and deleting its zero block. The addition and zero identities give the cosimplicial identities. Therefore the finite rational duals $U_{m,n}=(P_m^n)^*$ form a simplicial module. Its degeneracies insert zero blocks. Every tuple has a unique ordered list of nonzero blocks, so insertion of its zero blocks gives exactly the direct-sum decomposition indexed by order-preserving surjections required by [lem-sfb-split-simplicial-nondegenerate-homotopy]. The nondegenerate summand $V_{m,n}$ is the span of dual tuples with every block nonzero (and the empty tuple for $m=0,n=0$).

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of the rational polynomial-bar contraction; divided monomials and the actual splitting of U_m

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-simplicial-nondegenerate-homotopy] to this splitting over $R=\mathbf Q$, and dualize the chain maps and homotopies. Every term is finite dimensional, so the double dual identifies with the original polynomial component. Thus $P_m$ is cochain homotopy equivalent to $V_m^*$. The projected differential in $V_m$ merges two adjacent nonzero blocks with sign $(-1)^a$ for $1\leq a\leq n-1$; the end faces of a nonzero-block tuple are zero, since the dual outer cofaces have zero blocks. Consequently $V_m^*$ is the polynomial subcomplex $N_m$ spanned by the divided monomials with no zero block: its differential splits one block into two nonzero blocks with sign $(-1)^a$. There are no terms in $N_m^n$ for $n>\sum_i m_i$ when $m\ne0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of the rational polynomial-bar contraction; normalization and its exact projected differential

proof.text:
For $m\ne0$, send a nonzero-block tuple $(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$ to its cumulative partial sums
$$v_a=\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_a,\qquad1\leq a<n.$$
These are precisely the strict chains $0<v_1<\cdots<v_{n-1}<m$ in the coordinatewise interval; differences recover the tuple, so this is a bijection of bases, including $n=1$ and the empty chain. Merging blocks $a,a+1$ deletes $v_a$. The vertex-deletion sign is $(-1)^{a-1}$, whereas the merging sign is $(-1)^a$. Hence the differential on $V_{m,n}$ is the negative of the differential on $A(m)_{n-2}$ in [lem-sfb-product-chain-proper-interval-homology]. This minus sign does not change kernels or images. The lemma gives homology zero unless $m$ is squarefree, and in that case dimension one only for $n=\sum_i m_i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of the rational polynomial-bar contraction; interval identification, degree shift n-2, and the homology input

proof.text: A finite rational matrix and its transpose have the same rank (row and column reduction both reduce it to an identity block and zeros). In degree $n$, the homology dimension of $V_m$ and the cohomology dimension of $V_m^*$ are therefore both $\dim V_{m,n}-\operatorname{rank}\partial_n-\operatorname{rank}\partial_{n+1}$. With the preceding homotopy equivalence, $H^n(P_m)$ has the dimensions just found. For $m=0$, the nondegenerate complex has only $\mathbf Q$ in degree zero, so the same equivalence gives $H^0(P_0)=\mathbf Q$ and zero in other degrees. Give $e_I$ multidegree $1_I$. Since $pi=1$ and $i,p$ are cochain maps, their induced maps on each multidegree have composite the identity; in each nonzero cohomology degree both sides have dimension one, and in every other degree both sides vanish. Hence $p:P_m\to K_m$ induces an isomorphism in every degree, with inverse induced by $i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of the rational polynomial-bar contraction; finite ranks and the specified representatives

proof.text: Put $C_m=\ker(p:P_m\to K_m)$. The equations $pi=1$, $di=0$, $pd=0$ give a direct-sum decomposition of complexes $P_m=i(K_m)\oplus C_m$. For a cycle $c\in C_m^n$, the cohomology isomorphism proved above gives $c=db$ in $P_m$; replacing $b$ by $b-ipb$ puts it in $C_m$ and leaves $db$ unchanged. Thus $C_m$ is acyclic. Let $Z_m^n=\ker(d:C_m^n\to C_m^{n+1})$. By [lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement], choose $L_m^n$ with $C_m^n=Z_m^n\oplus L_m^n$. The restriction $d:L_m^n\to Z_m^{n+1}$ is injective because $L_m^n\cap Z_m^n=0$, and surjective because $Z_m^{n+1}=dC_m^n=dL_m^n$. For $z+l\in Z_m^n\oplus L_m^n$ define $h(z+l)$ as the unique inverse image of $z$ in $L_m^{n-1}$. In degree zero $Z_m^0=0$ by acyclicity and $C_m^{-1}=0$, so this prescription gives $h^0=0$. It satisfies $dh(z+l)=z$ and $hd(z+l)=l$. Set $h=0$ on $i(K_m)$ and take the direct sum over $m$. Then $dh+hd=1-ip$ on $P_{\mathbf Q,r}$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent proof of the rational polynomial-bar contraction; constructing the homotopy for the fixed i and p

proof.text: Each basis monomial belongs to one $P_m^n$, and its image under $h$ is an element of the ordinary polynomial space $P_m^{n-1}$, hence a finite rational linear combination of monomials. Use the same coefficient matrices over every commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra $B$: multiply the rational entries by the given coefficient in $B$. The differential, $i$, and $p$ have the same monomial formulas, so the rational identities remain equalities of finite coefficient sums over $B$. No exactness of scalar extension is needed. This also treats the zero algebra. If $r=0$, all terms are $B$, $d^n=0$ for even $n$ and $d^n=1$ for odd $n$. One may take $h^n=1$ for even $n\geq2$ and $h^n=0$ otherwise; then $dh+hd=1-ip$ in positive degrees and both sides vanish in degree zero. Thus the stated constant-complex edge case is included.

Steps 1-8 are verified. d^2 follows from the cosimplicial identities. di=0 holds as a cup product of 1-cocycles. pd=0 holds because the quadratic merged-block terms cancel in the wedge and repeated indices vanish. Divided-monomial multidegree components are finite and form a split dual simplicial module: zero-block insertion gives the splitting indexed by surjections. The Mathlib leaf homotopyEquivNondegComplex (SplitSimplicialObject.lean:148/165/307-312, needs only Preadditive) matches the new mathlib node. N_m (monomials with no zero block) is a subcomplex dual to the merge differential. Partial sums give a bijection with the strict chains of T_m, with sign -1 and degree shift n-2. Transpose rank, pi=1 and equal dimensions make i_* and p_* inverse isomorphisms. A complement-of-cycles homotopy (lem-trf-vector-subspace-complement) gives dh+hd=1-ip, and rational matrices extend to any B. The new node product-chain-proper-interval-homology is true: if some m_j>=2 the max(v,e_j) cone contracts it; if m is squarefree it is the subdivided boundary of a simplex, a sphere of dimension s-2; s=1 gives H_{-1}=Q. It is a separate combinatorial input and does not restate the item. split-simplicial is not a duplicate of lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence (Moore kernels versus a supplied splitting).
